about: The inaugural edition was launched on 08th March 2016, International Women’s Day, to highlight and applaud the role of women in resolving conflicts, be it at the level of family, community, society, intrastate or interstate. The cover story of this edition is an article on Women’s role in conflict resolution with case study on DURGA India – a community based initiative run by an NGO named I’m Every Women, wherein issues like sexual harassment and crime against women & girls are addressed. The other articles reflect on the 150 glorious years of Mahatma Gandhi. Father of not only our nation but also a universal acknowledged leader of peace, tolerance and Non-Violence. His ideals have inspired millions and will continue to do so. This year’s edition has articles based on his principles and ideas. UN International Day of Non-violence is celebrated all around the world on the 2nd October, as a tribute to him. His mammoth contributions to humanity will keep inspiring and guiding us.

This volume encapsulates articles based on women issues & their rights. Women  represent half of the humanity and yet this half is underrepresented in various activities. Be it in the political, economic, scientific or engineering realms. Even in the so called hi-tech countries, like Saudi Arabia, women are still fighting for their right for representation be it in parliament or top notch corporate jobs or even in their own families or tribes or clans. In the year 2011, Saudi Arabia finally granted right to vote to its women citizens. But  there remians a long way for their  genuine & true representation in all walks of life. The day when they are  given their due rights, the world will certainly be a just, fair, developed & progressive place. This annuaul edition is also unique as only women writers have contributed.

This volume has a few collection of articles contributed by students of Amity Institute of International Studies, Noida(Delhi- NCR) ,relating to the African sub-continent, countries of Ethiopia, Sudan and how Regional trade can bring about  peace in the war torn continent. A few articles of this issue also focus on the conceptual understanding of  Confidence Building Measures (CBMs)as peace tools in the India-Pakistan context.

This is a special edition featuring the Political science Masters students of St.Xaviers college, Ranchi. The edition endeavours to highlight the different social and political movements which took place in India with special reference to Jharkhand. The students have showcased their academic  writing skills by bringing about different aspects of social and political movements, legal rights of women, formation of new states such as Jharkhand and Chattisgarh and civil movements to foster peace in a conflict ridden state. Feminist movements, including legal & political rights for women, regional identity, role of Birsa Munda in Jharkhand movement.

The publication features articles on the effects of the COVID-19 Pandemic on achieving the Sustainable Development Goals(SDGs) in India as well as South Asia and the coping mechanisms used both at  the govenmental and the non governmental level.
The volume has articles on the conflicts, ensuing crisis situation in India's Neighbourhood. And also South Asian's women role as entrepreneurs in attaining sustainable goals.

This volume engages the readers with the peacebuilding and post conflict resonstruction activities of the conflict ridden countries in the South Asian sub-continent, inlucidng the North East Indian States.

Explore the intricacies of global peace efforts in our latest edition, "Exploring Treaties and Reports." This collection of articles critically assesses the effectiveness and challenges of key treaties and reports, offering valuable insights into the dynamic field of peace and conflict resolution.
This volume is based on interviews and conversations with renowned academics, social activists, policy makers, defence personnel  in the field of conflict, peace & security studies.
This edition includes the summary report of the 2nd OIJPCR Peace Conclave 2025 held on 31st Jan 2025 and climate themed interview based articles.
